Rigorous

RIG-er-us — contains 'rigor,' strict thoroughness; a rigorous test leaves nothing unchecked. · adjective

What It Means

Rigorous is extremely thorough, careful, or demanding.

Only the most dedicated applicants survived the university's rigorous admissions process.

Worked Example

Before a new medicine can be sold, it must pass through years of testing: careful trials on cells, then animals, then thousands of human volunteers, with every single result checked and rechecked by multiple independent teams.

A process this thorough, careful, and demanding at every single step is exactly what makes it rigorous. Unlike 'quick,' which values speed, rigorous values thoroughness above all else, even if it takes far longer.

How Rigorous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

thorough

thorough: complete and careful in every detail

stringent

stringent: strict and demanding, allowing no exceptions

exacting

exacting: demanding great care, effort, or attention

Antonyms

lax

lax: not strict or demanding enough

careless

careless: not giving enough care or attention

How Strong Is It? — careful → rigorous → exhaustive

careful vs. rigorous

careful vs. rigorous: Careful is a milder word than rigorous — being careful just means paying attention, while rigorous implies an extremely strict and demanding level of thoroughness.

exhaustive vs. rigorous

exhaustive vs. rigorous: Exhaustive can feel even more intense than rigorous: rigorous means strict and thorough, but exhaustive means leaving absolutely nothing at all unchecked or unexamined.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — rig-

root — rig-: stiff (Latin)

suffix — -orous

suffix — -orous: full of, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin rigor ('stiffness, harshness') comes from rigere, 'to be stiff.' A rigorous process is, at its root, full of unbending strictness that allows no shortcuts.
